mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side weakness, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both > 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate sales expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both > 6-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 7% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth) above its 12-month average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced marginal propensity to consume, which weakens demand and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 12-month MA for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 45% of triggered episodes.
